## Personality

Jane Andrews is a plain, sensible, and unflappable individual who carries out her pursuits in a practical, plodding, and conscientious manner. Described as nice and lady-like, she maintains a strict discipline when teaching. Her aims in her career are to earn her salary fairly, satisfy the trustees, and earn a place on the School Inspector's roll of honor, having once declared an intention to devote her entire life to teaching rather than marriage.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. ## History

Jane Andrews earned a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor and taught school in [Newbridge](../codex/places.md#newbridge). As a student, she accompanied [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and [Billy](../character/billy.md) to a recital at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), sharing compliments with [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) and expressing envy of the wealthy hotel guests during their ride home. After moving to town to attend Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy), Jane visited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) at her boarding house alongside [Josie](../character/josie-pye.md) and Ruby to help comfort her homesickness. Prior to starting their respective teaching positions, Jane joined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) in a debate regarding whether corporal punishment is ever necessary in school. She later took part in a spring picnic walk with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md), exploring new paths and discussing [Hester Gray](../character/hester-gray.md) in her forgotten garden. Active in local community efforts, Jane also accompanied [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) when they attempted to persuade [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) not to allow advertisements to be painted on his fences.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P1](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P34](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0034), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P38](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0038), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. ## Quotes

> "but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> "I’ll whip my pupils when they’re naughty. It’s the shortest and easiest way of convincing them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P14](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0014)

> "I suppose you won’t punish the girls by making them sit with the boys?"
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P23](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0023)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--jane-andrews.md)

Jane and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) share a long-standing friendship that dates back to their school days. They participate together in childhood games, school projects, and outings, such as traveling to a concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel). While Jane expresses envy over the wealthy guests at the hotel, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) holds a different perspective on contentment, though their bond remains intact through their shared experiences.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P2](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P17](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), +8 more_
